page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware-accelerated features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions. This server does not bundle local storage or GPU accelerators, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 138.13 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 24.29 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks achieve average performance, with gzip compression at 28.16 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 12.15 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, the c2d-highmem-2 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suited for lightweight database operations, text processing, and basic web serving, though its low database operations score and poor Redis SET performance suggest it is best reserved for non-intensive or development environments. It can also handle small-scale language model text generation, achieving an average speed of 79.09 tokens per second on a 135M model.
